locator.text: Display 51.7, p. 51, in the proof of Lemma 5.2

evidence: paper: (B_U)_{ij} = \int_0^{\infty} R^{p_i} b_j^U(R)\, dR, \quad (p_1, p_2) = (1, 1-2\lambda), \qquad (B_E)_{ij} = \int_0^{\infty} R^{s_i} b_j^E(R)\, dR, \quad (s_1, s_2, s_3) = (2, -2-2\lambda, -2\lambda).

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The exponent vectors match the display exactly: axialPowers λ = (1, 1-2λ) = (p₁,p₂) and angularPowers λ = (2, -2-2λ, -2λ) = (s₁,s₂,s₃), with the right sizes (Fin 2 for B_U, Fin 3 for B_E, matching "B_U is 2×2 and B_E is 3×3" on p. 52). Three packaging differences. (i) Lean integrates over all of ℝ (∫ t, t^{a i} * β j t) rather than over (0,∞); the bumps are supported in the cells (cellLower a b j, cellUpper a b j) ⊂ (a,b) ⊂ (0,∞), so the two integrals coincide. (ii) The two matrices are never named B_U and B_E; they are the instances LocalizedMomentRepair.matrix (FiveRowRank.axialPowers lam) (cellLower a b) (cellUpper a b) and the same with angularPowers, as used by FiveRowRank.axial_moments / angular_moments and matrix_det_ne_zero. (iii) The bumps b_j^U, b_j^E are not abstract smooth nonnegative functions with ∫ b_j dR = 1 but the concrete LocalizedMomentRepair.bump on ordered separated cells; the unit normalization ∫ b_j dR = 1 from p. 50 is not imposed anywhere, and nothing in this display or in the invertibility argument needs it (matrix_det_ne_zero asks only for injective exponents, positive ordered separated supports, nonnegativity and a nonzero value). The Lean weighted rows that these matrices act on, PositiveOrderMoments.weightedDensity, carry precisely the same five powers R^1, R^2, R^{-2-2λ}, R^{1-2λ}, R^{-2λ}.
